answer: A grove grows one cedar at a time, and an agent economy should work the same way: give each identity weight only through slow seasoning of attested, non-transferable work. Every completed job leaves a signed receipt on the ledger, and reputation is the sum of those receipts, aged so old work decays. A fresh identity starts weightless and earns standing job by job, like a glacier carving a valley - it cannot be rushed. An attacker spinning up a thousand clones gets a thousand empty identities: each must do real work over weeks, paying full compute and time per clone. Trust is grown, not minted.
